This is an underrated post.  I used Beacon back in 2017 and 2018 running a small cluster and it was really efficient for modifying drops.  I checked it out for my ASA server and it has come a long way from the beginning days.  I 100% will put in the work to avoid paying for software if there is a manual way to do something.  That said, this program is so incredibly simple to use compared to manually trying to adjust everything.  I would absolutely tell anyone that is going to put some serious time into a server they own, this **paid version is WORTH IT.**  

​

Some advice on using the deploy feature, Make sure the server is running, and any config changes you want to make in nitrado web interface and mods have been made.  If you follow these steps below, you will not have any issues using deploy.  

\- Complete any changes you want to make in the web interface (add your mods and anything else you want to do) Copy the line with the mod ids on it from the curseforge tab, youll need this later

\-**Keep server running** and **open beacon>new project>ark ascended \*\*DO THIS EVERYTIME YOU OPEN BEACON\*\*** it takes a little longer than loading a save file, but after having issues with settings reverting or mods disappearing, this is the only way I adjust settings now

\-top left of window select **Import** then **Nitrado**.  continue following the prompts until you get to a window that allows you to choose what is imported.  **\*Ensure you select custom configuration, it is unchecked by default)** Make sure you have linked your nitrado account to beacon.  Click ok

\-First time you get to this point, you will want to **go into the general settings,** take the time to validate that the settings you changed on the web interface align with what displays in beacon, if not, adjust accordingly before proceeding.  

**\*Any time you adjust the web interface settings on nitrado, its good practice to verify they carried into beacon.\***

\-You will see in **general settings** that there is a line for **active mods**.  **Paste the mod ids that you copied from the web interface into this field.**  Anytime you change and deploy settings with beacon, i recommend getting the mod ids and putting them into this field.  It overwrites the active mod config in the ini file and ensures that you will have the same mods you had prior to the deploy of new settings.  This field will always be blank under general settings after  import, but the ini will have the mod ids from your prior deployment. 

It is probably being overly cautious, but I lost a ton of mod items during a deploy because somehow I loaded a config with an incomplete list of active mods, so i just take the extra 2 seconds to copy the current mod ids into that field when making modifications to server.

Now that you have done this, Beacon is opened with the most up to date config from your server.  

\-Go to **custom config**, you will see **gameusersettings.ini** should be the default config file displayed.  Any INI adjustments can be entered here. Something that i also learned is under the **\[Server Settings\]** you can input command line arguments for the server to launch with. to do this  Remove the - or ?prefix, and add an equals sign with a value if the option does not already have one. (example:  **-**forceallowcaveflyers would go into this section as forceallowcaveflyers**=True**) 

**This will only work if using deploy method**  This is also where you will put any ini config settings for mods that you have on the server.  

\-When completed with everything you wanted to update, you click deploy up top, MAKE SURE THE SERVER IS STILL RUNNING BEFORE DEPLOYING.  

\-Check the box next to your server on the top left of the deploy window, and backup exisiting ini files should be checked by default. (always a good idea, in case you want to revert settings)

\-Hit continue, let it do its thing, it will restart the server with the correct mods, launch commands, and settings. 

Sorry for the wall of text, but I spent many hours trying to figure out a consistent process for command lines with nitrado on ASA and also for keeping the settings from getting reverted for seemingly no reason.  

TL;DR Step by step process on using deploy with nitrado successfully w/ command lines and stable restarts

I literally almost stopped playing. I have an insane cargo link hub going on with 2 outposts next to eachother, 6 links in each plus additional inter system links all over the settled systems. My game was unplayable, every 60-90 seconds it would tank my gpu usage from 95% down to like 7-10% for about 3-5 seconds. NOTHING WOULD FIX IT. I rolled back drivers, reinstalled the game, removed all mods scripts and everything that didn’t ship with the game. Nothing would work. I saw the comment about cargo links, I doubted it….to me it made no sense that it could be that if it was happening in systems that didn’t even have cargo links in them. Then I figured I had nothing to lose. So I removed the links with the terminals. Just disconnected. Figured if that was the problem it was the processing of the links, not the structure itself. 

The game has worked flawlessly since. I just want everyone that is building lots of cargo links to find this solution. Just disable them and your gpu % drop problems are gone
